claims.text: The proposed W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf refractory high-entropy alloy is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The initial alloy is nominally random and contains no long-range precipitates.
Cr-Hf pairs exhibit strong attractive chemical short-range ordering in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloys.
Cr-Hf attraction is driven by a strong negative enthalpy of mixing.
The W-Ta binary has a negative enthalpy of mixing.
Annealing between approximately 600 K and 1000 K is sufficient to activate diffusion and evolve the alloy from a random distribution to clustered SRO without macroscopic phase separation.
Chemical order between Cr and Hf vanishes at approximately 1080 K for W29.4Ta42Cr5.0V16.1Hf7.5.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit high thermal stability at elevated temperatures.
Annealing can produce a percolating Cr-Hf-rich or W-Ta-rich SRO network while retaining a single BCC phase.
The percolating ordered network has phonon dispersion characteristics distinct from those of the disordered matrix.
At low SRO density, isolated clusters increase phonon scattering through mass and strain-field fluctuations and thereby reduce thermal conductivity.
After SRO clusters percolate, the ordered network behaves as a coherent domain with reduced scattering cross-sections for selected phonon modes.
The percolating ordered network provides a low-scattering phonon pathway that bypasses scattering in the disordered matrix.
Increasing SRO produces a non-monotonic thermal-conductivity response consisting of an initial decrease followed by a sharp increase or anomalously high plateau.
The conductivity increase or plateau coincides with the connectivity threshold of the SRO clusters.
Above the SRO percolation threshold, thermal conductivity exceeds the value predicted by standard series, parallel, or effective-medium models.
Standard effective-medium and random-scattering simulations predict a monotonic conductivity decrease as SRO increases.
The proposed effect requires SRO-driving interactions strong enough to produce connected clusters but not strong enough to cause macroscopic precipitation or a crystal-structure transformation.
The predicted percolation threshold and conductivity increase depend on whether the interatomic potential energy surface accurately represents SRO energetics.
The hypothesis would be falsified by monotonic conductivity loss through the observed connectivity transition or by agreement with standard mixing models within experimental error.
